newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Mercury predicts power shakedown in next year.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Mercury predicts power shakedown in next year.

text.p: The chief executive of New Zealand power company Mercury Energy said in the company's annual report published on Wednesday that a flurry of alliances and mergers was likely in the sector this year.
"Developments can be expected in the coming year as the shakedown in the number of power companies operating in New Zealand continues," Wayne Gilbert said in the unlisted company's annual review.
Mercury plans to take joint control of its Auckland-based rival Power New Zealand after teaming up with fellow suitor Utilicorp NZ, controlled by Utilicorp United Inc.

Mercury and Utilicorp have formed a joint venture company and Gilbert said he believed that the benefits of joint control and subsequent operating rationalisation "will amount to about two-thirds of what they would have been with a full merger".
"The two Auckland companies combined (Mercury and Power NZ) will have approximately 24 percent of New Zealand's electricity distributions and five percent of power generation," he added.
By resolving the ownership battle with Utilicorp over Power NZ, Gilbert said Mercury believed the way would be cleared for "further definitiion of the market make-up".
